question: Your CI pipeline uses Claude Code to review pull requests in three categories: security, null-handling bugs, and naming conventions. A spot check of last month's findings shows false-positive rates of 6% for security, 9% for null-handling, and 68% for naming conventions, while security produces the most findings overall. Developers on several teams now ignore every Claude Code finding, including accurate security findings. Which change should you make first?

options.text: Replace the naming-convention category with a broader code-style category that also covers formatting, comment wording, and file layout.
options.reason: A broader, vaguer category moves away from explicit criteria, keeps noisy findings reaching developers, and does nothing to restore their trust.

options.text: Temporarily disable the naming-convention category, keep security and null-handling active, and re-enable the naming-convention category after its rewritten criteria pass testing.
options.reason: Temporarily disabling the one high false-positive category restores developer trust in the accurate categories while you improve the prompt for that category.

options.text: Keep all three categories active, and add an instruction to the review prompt telling Claude Code to be conservative about naming-convention findings.
options.reason: The guide says general instructions like "be conservative" fail to improve precision compared to specific categorical criteria.

options.text: Temporarily disable the security category because it produces the most findings, and keep the null-handling and naming-convention categories active.
options.reason: Finding volume is not the cause of the lost trust, so the noisy naming-convention category keeps undermining trust and accurate security findings are lost.
